name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Executive SMG ESM-2 'Attaché'
description:
The ESM-2 Attaché is disguised as a corporate briefcase. The weapon is permanently integrated into a standard Arcturus executive carry case, with the barrel concealed behind a false panel that deploys on BCI command. The operator carries the briefcase normally, and upon neural activation, the front panel drops, exposing the barrel and trigger assembly. The weapon fires through the opened panel while the operator holds the case by its handle.

Chambered in 4.6mm caseless with a 20-round internal magazine, the Attaché provides 3 seconds of automatic fire at 700 rpm. The BCI link handles targeting through the executive carry case's integrated sensors — the operator does not aim in any conventional sense. They point the case and the onboard system manages fire distribution across the threat zone.

Arcturus developed the Attaché for executives who travel through hostile territory and require personal defense capability that is genuinely invisible. The weapon passes standard security scans when the case is closed — the components are distributed through the case's structure in a pattern that mimics ordinary electronics. At Φ15,000, the Attaché is among the most expensive SMGs in production, but its customers have expense accounts.
specifications:
caliber: 4.6mm caseless
effective_range: 30m
rate_of_fire: 700 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds (internal)
weight: 2.5 kg (complete case)
tactical_use: The Attaché is a single-use emergency weapon. Its 20-round internal magazine provides one engagement's worth of firepower — enough to neutralize an immediate threat and create space for evacuation. The scan-defeating design allows the weapon to enter spaces where all visible weapons are prohibited, providing defense where it would otherwise be impossible. Once deployed, the disguise is blown and the case must be reloaded by Arcturus technicians.
cultural_context: The Attaché is an open secret in corporate executive circles. Everyone knows Arcturus makes a weapon disguised as a briefcase. No one knows who carries one. This uncertainty is itself a deterrent — any Arcturus executive's briefcase might contain a weapon, which means threatening any Arcturus executive carries a specific risk. The weapon's existence has influenced corporate fashion; some executives carry deliberately oversized briefcases as a bluff.
story_hooks: An executive's Attaché deployed accidentally during a board meeting when a BCI glitch interpreted a stressful negotiation as a threat response. No one was hit, but the footage is now leverage.
A counterfeit Attaché has appeared on the black market — it looks identical to the genuine article but contains a bomb instead of a weapon, targeting executives who trust the Arcturus brand.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek executive briefcase indistinguishable from high-end corporate carry luggage — perfectly mimics premium business aesthetics with subtle ergonomic curves and professional geometry. Only upon activation does the weapon nature become apparent as the front panel retracts to reveal a compact polymer SMG chassis integrated into the case structure.
physical_description.dimensions: Case: 42cm W × 30cm H × 12cm D. Integrated barrel assembly: 18cm concealed within front panel cavity. Total deployed weapon length from handle grip point: approximately 38cm when panel open.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively hefty for its size — 2.5kg distributed across the entire case structure creates balanced, professional carry feel. The weight suggests valuable cargo without betraying mechanical components. Handle accommodates one-handed carrying despite integrated systems.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum chassis with carbon-composite internal framework for component distribution. External synthetic leather facing with reinforced polymer panels. Barrel assembly: hardened steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal gray synthetic leather exterior with brushed aluminum trim. Internal barrel and mechanism show bare steel with light grease patina. Front panel interior (concealed until deployment) shows industrial polymer with precision machining marks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Professional charcoal gray and brushed silver with minimal branding. Accent: subtle Arcturus logo in matte black near handle. Internal components visible only when deployed — burnished steel and polymer black.
physical_description.grip_texture: Executive carry handle wrapped in conditioned synthetic leather with subtle grip-enhancement weave. Trigger assembly emerges from case structure with textured polymer for positive engagement despite integrated mounting.
distinctive_features: Motorized front panel with millisecond deployment mechanism
Concealed barrel outlet disguised as ventilation grille until activation
Integrated sensor array distributed across top surface (appears as subtle textured panels)
BCI interface contact points subtly recessed into handle underside
Internal magazine cavity molded into case bottom — no external magazine ports
Heat dissipation grilles integrated into side panels (appear as design elements)
Cable routing channels mimicking professional cable management
Mechanical detents disguised as latch mechanisms
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo embossed in matte black near handle. Serial number engraved on underside of handle in small, professional font. Model designation 'ESM-2' appears only on concealed internal barrel assembly plate. Regulatory compliance marking on interior surface (normally hidden).
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-pristine when in active service — the disguise depends on flawless appearance. Well-maintained internal mechanisms with light operational wear. After deployment, the case typically shows stress fractures around panel deployment mechanism and cosmetic damage to briefcase finish.
